 Ebrovisión 
 Ebrovisión 2027 will run from 2 to 5 September in Miranda de Ebro and passes are already on sale
 Redacción ModoFestival · Editor: Lucas Moreno 
 24 Oct 2026, 11:30 
 A 3-minute read 
 Katxo Bitxo / Ebrovisión, vía Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) 
 Follow us on Google 
 In short
 Ebrovisión 2027 will run from Thursday 2 to Sunday 5 September in Miranda de Ebro , with the same four-day format as in 2026 and more than ten months to plan the trip. 
 The general pass costs €67.50 and covers the paid nights on Friday 3 and Saturday 4 ; Thursday and Sunday are free, according to the ticket listing. 
 The full pass, the only one that included the surprise concerts at the castle, has already sold out : it was gone by 10 September, four days after the 2026 edition ended. 
 Anyone buying now does so without knowing a single name on the line-up , as the festival has not announced any artists or stage times for 2027. 
 Ebrovisión has started selling its 2027 edition before announcing a single artist. The festival in Miranda de Ebro (Burgos) will take place from 2 to 5 September 2027 , according to its official website, and the general pass is already on sale for €67.50 . The full pass, the most complete option, sold out in September.
 Festival guide 
 Ebrovisión 2027 
 2–5 Sep 2027 · Miranda de Ebro 
 Tickets 
 Disponibles 
 Ebrovisión 2027: 2 to 5 September
 The homepage of the festival's website bids farewell to the previous edition with a “Thank you!” and a date: “See you from 2 to 5 September 2027”. The dates run from Thursday to Sunday , the same format as the 2026 edition, which took place from 3 to 6 September and, according to the outlet Nosoloindie, drew 24,000 people over its four days.
 Ebrovisión is not concentrated in a single venue. In 2026 it spread its concerts across the main site at the Polideportivo de Anduva , the castle, the Anfiteatro Natural de la UBU, the Río Ebro stage and several streets and squares in Miranda. For 2027 the organisers have not yet given details of the stages, although the pass listing already places the festival at the Polideportivo Municipal de Anduva.
 Ty Segall at Ebrovisión 2017. Image: Katxo Bitxo / Ebrovisión, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0). General pass: €67.50 for Friday and Saturday
 The 2027 general pass is sold on Entradas.com , the ticketing platform the festival's website links to, for €67.50 including taxes. According to the notice on the listing itself, a service fee per order may be added, shown separately before payment, as well as delivery charges if physical delivery is chosen. ModoFestival may receive a commission if you buy through this link, at no extra cost to you.
 It is worth reading what is included before buying. The pass gives access to the nights of Friday 3 and Saturday 4 September ; Thursday 2 and Sunday 5 are free. It does not include the Castillo de Miranda stage , where the festival programmes a surprise performance that is not announced on the line-up.
 Minors may enter accompanied by their father, mother or legal guardian, who must sign a liability form. Children under 14 get in free.
 The full pass, sold out since September
 The other option, the full pass , added the concerts on the castle stage to the two paid nights. It can no longer be bought: Entradas.com lists it as sold out, and it has been since shortly after the 2026 edition. On 10 September, RockinBilbo ended its review with the full passes for 2027 “sold out”, and the following day Nosoloindie reported that a limited allocation had already sold.
 That a pass type sells out a year in advance and with no line-up speaks to the loyalty of Ebrovisión's audience, who buy for the festival rather than for the names. It also makes clear what anyone thinking of going should do: if the plan is Friday and Saturday, the general pass is currently the only option on sale to secure them.
 Still to be announced: line-up, stage times and stages
 The festival has not announced any artists for 2027. For reference, in 2026 Miranda hosted Lori Meyers , Rufus T. Firefly , Triángulo de Amor Bizarro and La Habitación Roja , alongside emerging acts and free concerts spread around the town. There are also no stage times or stage allocations yet, and the organisers have not said whether the general pass will go up in price.
 The Ebrovisión page covers how the previous edition went and will be updated with the 2027 edition, and the province's other events are in the festivals in Burgos listings.
 Sources: Ebrovisión official website and Entradas.com listing (2027 general pass and full pass), consulted on 24 October 2026; Nosoloindie, 11 September 2026; RockinBilbo, 10 September 2026.
